source_explicit: An integer dimension d and real spectral parameter kappa; indices i=1,...,d.
O is a real d-by-d orthogonal matrix. A=O Lambda O^T is the actual precision matrix; it is not the covariance.
f_A(x)=x^T A x/2 (called V_A in C.4); pi_A=N(0,A^(-1)); Z_A is the Gaussian normalizing constant.
direct_mathematical_inference: det Lambda is the finite product of the actual lambda_i, i=1,...,d; a d-dimensional diagonal determinant identity, not an additional source parameter.

source_explicit: The selected hard family assumes integer d>=2 and real kappa>=2, including d=2 and kappa=2.
O(d)={O in R^(d x d): O^T O=I_d}; this is the full real orthogonal group, not SO(d), a complex unitary group, or a determinant-conditioned component.
Real x in R^d. For every valid index: 0<theta_i<pi, -1<cos(theta_i)<1, and 1<lambda_i<kappa.
The ambient precision class is symmetric real matrices I_d<=A<=kappa I_d, in positive-semidefinite order.
direct_mathematical_inference: The actual Lambda and A are positive definite; det Lambda=det A>0. The powers in A3.Ex160 are ordinary real powers of positive real quantities. d/2 is real division, possibly a half-integer; (-1/2) is a real exponent.
domains.scope_caution: Section 2 permits ambient d>=1 and kappa>=1; that does not replace the selected S4.E11 hard-family hypotheses. The grid has strictly interior eigenvalues, although the admissible matrix class uses closed endpoint bounds.

source_explicit: For every integer d>=2 and every real kappa>=2, define the deterministic theta_i, lambda_i and Lambda.
For every O in O(d), form A=O Lambda O^T; the admissibility statement is universal in O.
The hard-input distribution draws O from Haar probability on the full O(d), independently of the algorithm private randomness.
For fixed Lambda, Z_A is independent of O; it is known whenever the spectrum is public.
direct_mathematical_inference: The determinant/product statement is pointwise for every orthogonal O and does not need a random draw or an almost-everywhere qualifier. There is no determinant-sign restriction.
quantifiers.scope_caution: No delta, epsilon, algorithm, query count, or large-d threshold belongs in the local algebraic determinant contract. Those occur in the separate main lower bound.

source_explicit: d>=2; kappa>=2; exact S4.E11 grid; O real orthogonal; A literally O Lambda O^T.
Spectrum public is a condition for the knowledge assertion, not a hypothesis needed for determinant invariance or the mathematical value of the normalizer.
proof_ingredients_not_additional_premise: Strict cosine/grid eigenvalue bounds, positive definiteness and positive determinant follow from the source construction.

Orthogonal determinant identities, diagonal determinant/product identity and Gaussian integration are dependencies to establish inside the corresponding proof; they must not become user-supplied conclusion-shaped assumptions.
Gaussian integrability/normalization for a positive definite real quadratic is mathematical content of an integral-level result, not something the source asks an algorithm to provide.
forbidden_unjustified_restrictions: large-d or kappa<=d^(1-delta) for this local component
assuming det A=det Lambda or assuming the target integral value as a binder

conclusion.bounded_determinant_component_direct_inf: For actual A=O Lambda O^T, det A=det Lambda=product_{i=1}^d lambda_i>0; this scalar depends on d,kappa through the fixed grid and is independent of O.
conclusion.source_explicit_knowledge_conclusion: Since Lambda is fixed, Z_A is independent of O and is known whenever the spectrum is public.
conclusion.reference_measure_inference: The intended unweighted normalizing integral is integral_{R^d} exp(-x^T A x/2) dx, with Euclidean Lebesgue measure. The selected C.4 text does not itself write this integral or explicitly name Lebesgue measure; this interpretation follows from its Gaussian-integration statement, potential, Gaussian target, and usual density convention.
not_interchangeable: The actual matrix determinant/product identity alone is not an integral evaluation.
A scalar defined by the displayed formula is not, merely by definition, proved equal to the unweighted integral.
Known Z does not imply that the full density at x is known from the spectrum alone.
This local component does not prove the full C.4 admissibility/smoothness/minimizer argument or the main query lower bound.

source_explicit: Full real O(d) has determinant +1 and -1 components, each Haar probability 1/2. The universal hard-family/admissibility claim covers both.
A is the precision of N(0,A^(-1)). Lambda and its spectrum are deterministic; O is the hidden random eigenbasis.
Independence of Z from O holds with d and kappa, hence Lambda, fixed.
mathematical_inferences: A density under the usual Euclidean convention is p_A(x)=Z_A^(-1)*exp(-x^T A x/2). Its quadratic factor generally depends on O, even though Z_A does not.

Unweighted Lebesgue integration must be distinguished from expectation under a normalized Gaussian reference measure or Haar probability. Changing the reference measure changes the normalizer identity.
No orientation-dependent absolute determinant factor remains: the actual conjugated precision determinant has det(O)^2=1. This does not require det(O)=+1.
outside_bounded_component: Full C.4 also establishes spectral admissibility, C-infinity regularity, Hessian A, 1-strong convexity, kappa-smoothness and unique minimizer 0.

Theorem 4.1 additionally has fixed delta in (0,1), d>=d0(delta), 2<=kappa<=d^(1-delta), 0<epsilon<=1/10, and a query lower bound delta*sqrt(kappa)*log(d)/256. These do not become local determinant assumptions or conclusions.

exact_constants: The unweighted Gaussian normalizer factor is (2*pi)^(d/2); determinant exponent is -1/2.
dependencies: The finite product det Lambda and the corresponding positive scalar normalizer depend on d and kappa via the fixed grid; they have no O-dependence.
No algorithm seed, query budget, epsilon or delta enters the bounded determinant/normalizer identity.
Public spectrum is sufficient knowledge of eigenvalues with multiplicities to compute the determinant and normalizer; no particular cost model for that computation is asserted here.
endpoints: 1<lambda_i<kappa for the selected family; 1 and kappa are comparison constants, not attained eigenvalues.
The source has no parity assumption: odd d makes d/2 half-integral.
